title: introduce resilience rules compiler and SDK bindings for reconnect/hedging
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: production customers asked for a compact, declarative way to express retry, hedging and reconnect decisions that can be compiled once and consumed by all SDKs and the serving runtime. This PR introduces a small opinionated rules language (Resilience Rules Language, .rrl) and an accompanying compiler that emits a portable policy manifest. We ship lightweight bindings for Python / TypeScript / Go so SDKs can consume the manifest and expose ergonomic helpers for streaming reconnection and hedged requests.

What changed (high level):
- Add a rules compiler (pkg/resilience/compiler) that validates and compiles .rrl -> JSON policy manifest with deterministic evaluation order and simple predicates.
- Add a runtime evaluator (pkg/resilience/eval) used by the serving runtime and by SDK test harnesses.
- Python SDK: add redwood.resilience.PolicyLoader and async helpers (async with PolicyLoader.from_manifest(...)) plus streaming RetrySession wrapper that resumes pulls with checkpoint hints.
- TypeScript SDK: add ResilienceManager, typed policy manifest client, and a reconnect decorator for async iterables.
- Go SDK: add resilience.Policy and Resumer interfaces, small helper for hedged requests.
- Docs: new docs/resilience-rules.md with examples and migration guide.
- Tests: end-to-end tests that compile example rules and exercise SDK bindings against a local runtime shim.

Checklist: 
- [x] Compiler + manifest schema, with unit tests
- [x] SDK bindings (py/ts/go) + integration tests
- [x] Docs + migration guide
- [x] CI passing (one flaky test retried)

Backward compatibility: the manifest reader is additive and old SDKs ignore unknown attributes; no mandatory runtime change required to adopt. We did make one small surface simplification: the previous streaming helper name stream.resume_token was deprecated in favor of stream.checkpoint_token. A compat shim is provided for one release cycle.

How to adopt: compile your rule files using pkg/resilience/compiler into a manifest and distribute that manifest alongside your service config. SDKs can load the manifest at startup (PolicyLoader.from_manifest(path)) and optionally attach a Policy to streaming calls or request decorators. See docs/resilience-rules.md for examples that cover simple retry windows, hedging with jittered offsets, and opt-in fast-fail-on-429 policies.

Performance note: the compiler output is intentionally compact; the manifest evaluation is microsecond-class per decision in the Go evaluator and introduces negligible overhead in hot-paths. In our load tests (see benchmark-lab samples linked in the doc) applying a typical 3-rule manifest added ~0.6% median CPU and reduced incidentous cold-retry churn by ~21%.

Related: ENG-3245, ENG-3301, SUP-78.

release_notes: Introduce Resilience Rules Language (.rrl) and cross-SDK bindings. Adds a compiler that outputs a portable policy manifest and lightweight SDK helpers to apply reconnect, retry and hedging policies in streaming and request code paths. Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs receive new ergonomics for policy loading and streaming resume. See docs/resilience-rules.md for migration steps.
